a2-unit-21.21.1 The Tortoise and the Hare:
Tom: OK, everyone, it's story time. Today's story comes from a very old book. It's called The Aesop for Children, and it was published right here in Chicago in 1919. Aesop was a storyteller in ancient Greece, more than 2,500 years ago. His stories are called fables. They're short, the characters are often animals, and at the end there's a lesson. Ready? This one is called The Tortoise and the Hare.
Tom: One day, a hare was watching a tortoise. He was laughing because the tortoise was so slow.
Tom: The hare said to the tortoise, "I can't believe you're going to get anywhere today. Can't you go any faster?"
Tom: The tortoise replied, "Don't worry. I'm faster than you think. Do you want to have a race?"
Tom: The hare thought this was a funny idea, but he agreed. They decided on the start and finish lines for the race. "Ready, set, go!" said the hare, and he ran off quickly.
Tom: The tortoise started too, but much more slowly. After a few minutes, the hare looked back. He didn't see the tortoise, so he decided to take a short rest under a tree.
Tom: While the hare was sleeping, the tortoise was walking as fast as he could. Soon, he passed the hare and continued toward the finish line.
Tom: The hare woke up. He was surprised to see that the tortoise was almost at the finish line. He ran as fast as he could, but he didn't catch the tortoise. The tortoise was the winner.
Tom: So, what do you think? What's the lesson of this story?
a2-unit-21.21.2 The Ants and the Grasshopper:
Tom: The Ants and the Grasshopper.
Tom: One fall, a family of ants was working in the sunshine. They were picking up food and saving it for the winter. A hungry grasshopper stopped to talk to them. He had a violin.
Tom: "Can I have something to eat, please?" asked the grasshopper.
Tom: The ants were surprised. "Why don't you have any food? What were you doing all last summer?"
Tom: The grasshopper answered, "I didn't have any time to look for food. I was playing music all summer on my violin."
Tom: The ants continued with their work. "We can't help you if you don't help yourself."

Narrator: was
Narrator: were
Narrator: The hare was watching the tortoise.
Narrator: The ants were working in the sunshine.
Narrator: What were you doing?
Narrator: While the hare was sleeping, the tortoise passed him.
Narrator: Was he sleeping? Yes, he was.
Narrator: Were they working? No, they weren't.
